title: Small quasicategory tests suffice in every larger universe
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix nested Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$. A simplicial set is $\mathcal U$-small when the disjoint union of its degree sets is bijective to a set in $\mathcal U$. For any simplicial set $S$, let $hS$ be the ordinary category with its vertices as objects and finite composable words of edges as morphisms, modulo the relations identifying degenerate edges with identities and identifying the long edge of each $2$-simplex with the composite of its two successive edges. Let $u:A\to B$ be a map of $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets. The following conditions are equivalent: (i) for every $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $C$, restriction induces an equivalence of ordinary categories $h\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$; (ii) the same assertion holds for every $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory $C$. No local $\mathcal U$-smallness hypothesis on the mapping spaces of the latter $C$ is imposed. The empty simplicial sets and empty quasicategories are included.

source.place: Agent-formulated universe refinement of the ordinary homotopy-category testing convention in Theorem 3.6.8(iii), printed pp.115-116 (July 30, 2026 revision); elementary finite-presentation/small horn-closure argument, not asserted there as a separate theorem. Source read online 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this comparison. WANTED: archived source in literature/.

proof.text: The implication from (ii) to (i) is immediate: every $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory is also $\mathcal V$-small, so the hypothesis in the larger testing universe includes the smaller testing family. The empty quasicategory is included because the quantifiers impose no nonemptiness condition.

source.place: Agent expansion of the universe-comparison argument following Theorem 3.6.8(iii), printed pp.115-116

proof.text: For the converse, fix a $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory $C$. If $X\subseteq C$ is a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial subset, [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion] supplies a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $RX$, a monomorphism $j_X:X\hookrightarrow RX$, and the restriction map $j_X^*:\operatorname{Fun}(RX,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,C)$ with the right lifting property against every monomorphism. Applying that lifting property to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$ extends every map $X\to C$ to a map $e:RX\to C$ with $e j_X$ equal to the given map. The same statement covers $X=\varnothing$ and $C=\varnothing$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the universe-comparison argument following Theorem 3.6.8(iii), printed pp.115-116

proof.text: Given any $\mathcal U$-small family of simplicial maps whose domains are $\mathcal U$-small, let $X$ be the simplicial subset of $C$ generated by all their simplex images. The union of their degreewise images and all faces and degeneracies is $\mathcal U$-small, so every map in the family factors through $X$. This also applies to a finite chain of edges and $2$-simplices witnessing an equality in an $h\operatorname{Fun}$ category. Thus all data used below can be placed in one such $X$, followed by the extension $e:RX\to C$ of step 2.

source.place: Agent expansion of the universe-comparison argument following Theorem 3.6.8(iii), printed pp.115-116

proof.text: Assume (i), and let $F:A\to C$ be a coherent functor. Choose $X$ from step 3 for the image of $F$, factor it as $A\xrightarrow{F_X}X\xrightarrow{j_X}RX$, and extend the inclusion $X\to C$ to $e:RX\to C$. Since $RX$ is a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory, (i) says that $h\operatorname{Fun}(B,RX)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(A,RX)$ is an equivalence. Its essential-surjectivity part gives $G:B\to RX$ whose restriction is isomorphic in $h\operatorname{Fun}(A,RX)$ to $j_XF_X$. Postcomposition with $e$ gives a functor $eG:B\to C$ and carries that isomorphism to one between its restriction and $F$. Hence restriction for $C$ is essentially surjective.

source.place: Agent expansion of the universe-comparison argument following Theorem 3.6.8(iii), printed pp.115-116

proof.text: For fullness, take $G,H:B\to C$ and a morphism in $h\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ from $G|_A$ to $H|_A$. Choose $X$ as in step 3 for the images of $G,H$ and for a finite edge-word representative of this morphism, and factor the data through $RX$ before extending to $C$. Hypothesis (i), applied to the $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $RX$, gives a morphism in $h\operatorname{Fun}(B,RX)$ whose restriction is the chosen class. Postcomposition with $e$ is the required morphism from $G$ to $H$ and has exactly the prescribed restricted class, because all representatives were included in $X$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the universe-comparison argument following Theorem 3.6.8(iii), printed pp.115-116

proof.text: For faithfulness, suppose two morphism classes in $h\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)$ have equal restrictions. Choose finite edge-word representatives for both and a finite chain of $2$-simplex relations in $h\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ witnessing equality of their restrictions. Put the images of every diagram, edge and relation simplex into one $\mathcal U$-small $X$ as in step 3, and factor the data through $RX$. The two resulting classes in $h\operatorname{Fun}(B,RX)$ have equal restrictions by that same relation chain. The faithfulness part of the equivalence in (i) makes them equal; postcomposition with $e$ then makes the original classes equal. Thus restriction for $C$ is fully faithful, and together with step 4 it is an equivalence. Since $C$ was arbitrary, (i) implies (ii), including empty inputs.

Steps 4-6: essential surjectivity, fullness and faithfulness for RX pass to C by e_*, which is a functor on h commuting with u^*; the finite relation chains lie in Fun(A,X).
